case.case_title: Rassool and others v. Cader, Director for Mosques and Muslim Charitable Trusts and others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1993] 2 Sri LR.

clause.text: No citizen shall be discriminated against on the grounds of race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth or any one of such grounds.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners were discriminated against on the ground of political opinion in violation of Article 12(2) by their suspension from office.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners alleged that their suspension was due to their political activities and opposition to the ruling party, constituting discrimination on the ground of political opinion.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied discrimination, asserting the suspension was due to misuse of Mosque premises for political purposes and not political opinion.
key_facts: The 1st petitioner was a candidate for the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress opposing the ruling United National Party.
The 1st respondent suspended the petitioners allegedly due to political activities within Mosque premises.
No evidence was produced that other Trustees with different political affiliations were treated similarly.
The petitioners bore the burden to prove discrimination on political grounds.
The court found no credible evidence that the 1st respondent had reasonable suspicion of misuse of Mosque premises.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(2) as prohibiting discrimination on political opinion and held that the burden of proof lies on the petitioners to establish such discrimination by a high degree of credibility.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the suspension was motivated by the petitioners' political opinions and activities, without reasonable suspicion or evidence of misuse of Mosque premises, thus constituting discrimination under Article 12(2).
principles_established: Discrimination on political opinion is prohibited under Article 12(2).
Burden of proof lies on the petitioner to establish discrimination with credible evidence.
Public officers acting without reasonable suspicion and suspending on political grounds violate fundamental rights.
precedents_cited: Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu AIR 1974 SC 555
Saman v. Leeladasa [1989] 1 Sri L R. 1

outcome.holding: The court declared that the petitioners' fundamental right under Article 12(2) was violated by the 1st respondent due to discrimination on political opinion and awarded compensation and costs.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of violation, compensation to petitioners, and costs payable by the 1st respondent.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(2) was dispositive in establishing that the suspension was discriminatory on political grounds, which was the core of the petitioners' fundamental rights claim.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court held that the 1st respondent suspended the petitioners on account of their political opinions and activities without reasonable suspicion, violating Article 12(2).
